name: Raahe
title: Raahe Steel Port Thickness Measurement: Bulk and Steel Ships
description: UTM in Raahe for bulk carriers bringing ore pellets, coal and limestone to the steel works and ships loading steel: hold, tank top and hatch cover gauging.
h1: Hull and Hold Gauging for Ships Serving the Raahe Steel Works
intro: Raahe's port exists largely for one customer: SSAB's integrated steel works on the shore beside it. Bulk carriers bring iron ore pellets, coal and limestone, and general cargo ships load hot-rolled strip, plate and coils for customers around the Baltic and beyond. Heavy raw materials and heavy finished steel both leave their mark on holds and tank tops, which is what gauging here is usually about. Technicians travel from India to Raahe for each job, with nobody stationed at the port.
keywords: bay of bothnia ice belt gauging

highlights.p: Few ports show both sides of a steel works so plainly. Bulk carriers discharge ore pellets, coal and limestone at the raw-material berths, while general cargo and multipurpose ships load steel, so the same port sees grab wear on one fleet and coil damage on another.

Coils and heavy plate concentrate their weight on small areas of the tank top, and dunnage, lashing and forklift work add their own damage. On the ships that load steel at Raahe, tank tops, hold frames and the double bottom below deserve close gauging.

SSAB has set out plans to move its Nordic steelmaking away from blast furnaces towards electric arc furnaces. If Raahe follows that route, the coal trade would give way to other raw materials, and the bulk tonnage calling here would change along with it.

port.h: The Port of Raahe and the steel trade
p: Raahe stands on the eastern shore of the Bay of Bothnia, south of Oulu, an old wooden trading town whose modern port grew with the steel works built beside it in the 1960s. The harbour at Lapaluoto, close to the works, has quays for bulk raw materials and for loading finished steel, and the works' stockyards, coke plant and blast furnaces sit a short haul away. Ships approach across shallow coastal water through a dredged fairway, and as on the rest of this coast the sea is practically tideless, with levels moving with wind and pressure. The old town, with its wooden houses, is a reminder of Raahe's past as a sailing-ship port, but nearly all of today's tonnage is industrial.

Inbound, the main cargoes are iron ore pellets, coal for the coke ovens and limestone, carried by bulk carriers of various sizes, many of them on short Baltic routes. Outbound, hot-rolled strip, plate and coils go to customers in Europe and further afield on general cargo, multipurpose and open-hatch ships, often on a regular loading pattern. Because the works runs continuously, raw-material deliveries are steady and the same ships return on regular contracts, which gives owners a predictable chance to have them gauged. Discharging ore and coal by grab and loading steel by crane are both deliberate operations, and ships typically stay alongside for a day or more, enough to fit a well-prepared gauging scope.

Ice closes in on Raahe every winter. The northern Bay of Bothnia freezes reliably, ships need ice classes that satisfy the Finnish winter traffic restrictions for the port, and icebreakers escort traffic in the hardest months. The works' supply chain cannot stop for the winter, so ice-class bulk carriers keep raw materials coming and steel keeps moving out, and their ice belts take the punishment. The open-water season is when bulk carriers without high ice classes can be used and when ships go to dock. A Raahe gauging job often falls at the turn of a season: in autumn, before a ship commits to winter trading, or in late spring, when the ice has gone and the damage can be assessed.

facilities.h: Gauging sites at the Raahe raw-material and steel berths
p: On the raw-material side, bulk carriers are gauged as they discharge. Ore pellets and coal leave fine abrasive dust and damp residues that hide pitting, so reading points are cleaned locally, and the lower parts of hold frames, brackets and hopper plating, where the grab works hardest, get a closer reading pattern. Topside and double-bottom tanks are entered once the crew has issued the enclosed-space permit. On the steel side, holds are measured before the stow is built, with particular attention to tank top plating under the coil rows and to the frames, brackets and lashing points that take cargo loads at sea.

We do not plan dockings in Raahe; ships on this trade dock at repair yards elsewhere in the Baltic, chosen by the owner. The useful role of Raahe comes earlier in the cycle: a ship that calls regularly can be measured at one or two calls before her docking, so the yard knows how much tank top, frame and ballast tank steel to prepare. Work at anchor is not part of our Raahe planning, because ships berth directly and in winter arrive under icebreaker escort.
list: Raw-material berths at Lapaluoto — bulk carriers discharging iron ore pellets, coal and limestone; hold, hopper and tank-top gauging as each hold empties
Steel loading quays — general cargo, multipurpose and open-hatch ships; tank-top and hold-frame gauging before the steel stow is built
Ballast tanks and double bottoms on both fleets — measured under the ship's permits during the cargo stay
Hatch covers and coamings — gauged on steel carriers, where weathertightness protects a cargo that rusts quickly
Repair yards elsewhere in the Baltic — in-dock follow-up of readings first taken at Raahe

context.h: Inspection, ice class and the steel trade's demands
p: Raahe is a Finnish port, so port state control is carried out by Traficom under the Paris MoU, and bulk carriers are among the ship types the regime targets more closely. Ice class is a practical condition of trade here: the Finnish winter traffic restrictions decide which ships may call and be assisted by icebreakers, and a ship whose ice belt has thinned below the class requirement risks the notation she needs for winter contracts. Bulk carriers fixed for Raahe through the winter are therefore checked by charterers for ice class, and owners are better placed with recent ice-belt readings to hand.

Steel receivers are particular about cargo condition. Hot-rolled steel that gets wet in the hold rusts and leads to claims, so the ships that load at Raahe need weathertight hatch covers, sound coamings and no leaks from ballast tanks or air pipes into the holds. Gauging of hatch cover plating, coamings and the hold boundaries with the ballast tanks addresses exactly that. On the raw-material side the ESP rules apply to the bulk carriers, so their renewal and intermediate surveys bring the full set of transverse sections and close-up survey requirements, and a Raahe discharge is a good place to begin that work.

jobs.h: Typical gauging jobs for ships at Raahe
jobs.p: Raahe jobs divide between the two fleets that serve the steel works. Bulk carriers bring hold and tank gauging for surveys, condition checks and steel planning, usually done during discharge so they never delay a delivery to the works. Steel carriers bring tank-top and hold-boundary gauging, often after a cargo claim or before a new contract, together with hatch cover work. Seasonal checks on the ice belt come at the start and the end of winter, and occasional pre-purchase jobs arise when one of the regular ships is sold. Every scope is agreed with the superintendent and the chief officer in advance, so the readings follow the cargo plan rather than fighting it.
list: ESP intermediate-survey gauging on a bulk carrier discharging iron ore pellets, covering holds, hoppers and selected ballast tanks
Tank-top and double-bottom gauging on a multipurpose ship before she loads steel coils at Raahe
Hatch cover and coaming gauging on a steel carrier after a wet-cargo claim, compared with the crew's own tightness test results
Pre-winter ice-belt gauging on an ice-class bulk carrier fixed to carry coal to the works through the winter
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a regular coal or ore carrier when she changes hands

logistics: Raahe has no scheduled airport, so the team flies from India to Helsinki and on to Oulu Airport, then drives south along the coast to Raahe. Our technicians travel on Schengen visas, and we begin the application as soon as the ship's arrival window is clear. Access to the berths at Lapaluoto and to the steel works' areas is arranged through the ship's agent, and the works' own safety rules and induction apply to everyone entering. In winter we allow a margin for road conditions and icebreaker delays.

faqs.q: Can you gauge bulk carriers during discharge at Raahe?
faqs.a: Yes. Holds are measured one by one as they are emptied, with tank tops, hopper plating, frames and brackets covered first because grab wear concentrates there. Ballast and topside tanks follow once the crew has issued entry permits. The aim is to finish within the discharge so the steel works' delivery schedule is not affected; anything left goes on the list for the ship's next call.

faqs.q: What damage do steel coils cause to a ship's holds?
faqs.a: Coils and heavy plate put high point loads on the tank top, and careless landing, dunnage and forklift work can dent plating and crack welds in the double bottom below. Lashing points and frames take loads in a seaway. We gauge tank top plating under coil rows, look for local thinning around dents, and add magnetic particle checks on suspect welds and lashing fittings.

faqs.q: Why gauge hatch covers on ships loading steel?
faqs.a: Hot-rolled steel rusts quickly if seawater or rain gets into the hold, and wet-damage claims follow. Hatch cover plating, coamings, cleats and seals keep the cargo dry, and corrosion in those areas causes leaks. Gauging hatch cover top plates, skirt plates and coamings, alongside the crew's own tightness tests, shows whether a leak is a seal problem or a steel problem.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Raahe?
faqs.a: Not one we plan around. Ships trading to Raahe dock at repair yards elsewhere in the Baltic, chosen by the owner. What Raahe offers is regular calls: a bulk carrier or steel carrier on contract to the works can be measured during one or two discharges before her docking, so the yard has a measured steel list in advance and the docking period is set realistically.

faqs.q: How does winter affect a Raahe job?
faqs.a: Inside the ship, little changes beyond ventilating spaces for longer and using couplant suited to the cold. Outside, ice against the hull limits shell readings alongside, and icebreaker escort can shift arrival times. We build a buffer into winter jobs, keep in contact with the agent daily, and suggest that any scope needing the outer shell is moved to the open-water season.
